Film di un'ora e un quarto circa che ci fa vivere dentro un incubo. Il film parte tranquillamente, colonna sonora tranquilla e scene che possono far pensare che il film sia qualcosa di non pesante da vedere. Circa però dopo la prima mezz'oretta parte il disastro; colonna sonora inquietante, ma molto bella, scene che ti fanno domandare se quello che stai vedendo ha senso, e un continuo farti credere che qualsiasi cosa che guardiamo sia vera, per poi rivelarsi falsa. Il film tocca temi difficile e soprattutto complicati, quindi per capire cosa vuole trasmettere questa pellicola l'unico modo è guardarlo. Voto indicativo: 7.6/10

Un des films les plus mindfuck que j’ai vu tant on se retrouve en constant questionnement sur la réelle nature des images. C’est une oeuvre assez unique, nous plongeant dans un dédale psychologique cauchemardesque. Une immense paranoïa où tout nous est pris, notre corps, notre personnalité, notre carrière. Je pense qu’il y’a dans cela une critique de la main mise de l’industrie sur les femmes, Satoshi Kon nous dépeint une protagoniste qui n’est jamais maître de ses actions, perdu et infantilisée, dans une société patriarcale où elle doit remplir les critères de validation masculine.
It’s not an easy watch for a whole host of reasons, but I can’t remember the last movie that managed to blur the lines between reality and fiction so effectively.

Sentí como que no llegaban a ninguna parte, solo estaban para tomarme el pelo. En medio, una historia que parecía sencilla, troca para bien o para mal. After a second viewing and knowing where it’s heading, it helped me appreciate all the subtle hints laid throughout its runtime, even if some details are still left up in the air.

Nice to rewatch this sober many years later (do not watch high, way too hallucinatory)  feels like seeing it with fresh eyes. anime Black Swan before that was a thing. If you think because it’s animated it won’t get you and fuck you up you’d be wrong. The stalking, and invasion of privacy the creeping parasocial relationship towards a celebrity not to mention the rape scene all get under your skin. I'm not really criticizing the animation as a failure -- I'm saying some of it is objectively goofy looking, but it also ended up being fucking hilarious and didn't stop me from getting immersed. That's different from a flaw that actively damages the movie for me lmao But all in all, Perfect Blue's writing is strong enough to carry basically any visual quirk. The way the film keeps fucking with your perception while still having an actual coherent psychological story underneath it is the real achievement. Also the imagery is incredible. Mirrors, reflections, screens, performances, the repeated imagery of Mima's face -- it constantly plays with the idea of looking at yourself versus being looked at by somebody else. The individual drawings might occasionally look a bit funny, but the composition and visual ideas are doing so much work. Very, very, very, very, VERY solid film.

A beautiful, astonishingly well-written exploration of the objectification of pop stars, the paranoia inherent to being a celebrity and being surrounded by potential enemies at all times, the psychological effects of being a woman and being surrounded by larger men who would be more than happy to rape you if the opportunity presented itself, the difference between our professional and personal personas and the troubles that can arise if those boundaries blur, and the jealousy older women have for younger women once their sexual value has subsided, all of it set at the dawn of the Internet (which has turned us all into mini-celebrities to some degree). I must confess at the outset that one of my big life goals is to become a pornographer. I've never wanted children, and after a few lucrative decades spent training for and then succeeding at high-paying Silicon Valley tech jobs, I am restless to spend my thirties becoming physically strong and sexually virile. I want to become extremely strong and create an OnlyFans where I make love to a succession of beautiful, ideally white, young women in both conventional and comedic scenarios, filmed POV. There's not much profit in it, but frankly, I already have enough money (for myself to live off, so don't get any bright ideas that I'm Richie Rich). The whole point of making money is to ultimately be able to do what you want with your life. Some men want to race cars, others to raise large families, others to hunt and fish. I want to direct adult films and be a stud. (I also have higher-minded, more conventional artistic goals as relates to my own people, the Hindus, but those might be more of a later-life thing. I have time.) I tell you this to make it clear that I'm not approaching Perfect Blue from a feminist angle. My view is that all of life, from the smallest bacterium to the blue whale, is an abattoir where the strong feast upon the weak. While fossil fuels allowed us a brief reprieve from Malthusian brutality for a short few centuries, our population has increased, our technology has stagnated, and our climate is changing to the point that the "law of the jungle" is once again taking hold. I view Perfect Blue as a chronicle of the return of Japanese civilization (and all civilization more broadly) to something more primal as humanity leaves our peak years behind us. My expectation is that humans in 2200 will envy the lifestyles of peasants in 1200. Mima is a pop idol trying to transition into becoming an actress. As an idol, she mostly performed for horny middle-aged men and local louts, and she hopes for a more dignified career as she ages. Ironically, her background and the changing times get her cast in "degrading" roles, and her breakout role is playing a stripper who gets raped by the crowd. (Don't mind that scribbling you hear in the background, I'm just taking notes for my own work.) She also strips for various photoshoots (to my pleasure, said shots show her vulva - director Satoshi Kon doesn't pussy out in the way Western directors would). Throughout the film, we're treated to various shots showing murders and such, only to then hear a director yelling "Cut!" and realize that it was just shots from her acting career. So when actors and directors associated with Mima start turning up dead and an ugly stalker obsessed with Mima arrives without any cameras around, we start to realize that Mima is in actual danger. Figuring out what's real and what isn't is most of the fun of the film's incredible plotting, and while I personally didn't like the happy ending and twist culprit (I think it would have been more interesting to see Mima raped and killed by a deranged stalker, frankly), I understand that normal audiences would not be okay with that, and poor Mr. Kon probably wouldn't be invited to direct more high-budget films. My personal ending is that the film fades to black as the stalker assaults Mima. I watched Perfect Blue in the theater on a lark when I happened to come across its listing on Fandango (I watched Paprika by Kon years ago and was not impressed, so it's unlikely I would have watched this on my own without the prod from the theater). I'm utterly thrilled with Cinemark for airing all these re-releases and remasters (there's a remaster of classic anime Angel's Egg later this year that I also can't wait to catch). Most new films are frankly trash (they're all remakes or sequels because our present reality is so shitty that there's no source material to make movies about). But there's happily enough great movies from civilization's peak that we could just air them all in a loop and have more than enough to satisfy a human lifetime.

Mind warping, gross, stressful. I say all of this as a compliment. It's insane and depressing how this movie's handling of the subject matter has only gotten more and more accurate through the years. The boundaries between celebrities and fans have only gotten blurrier, with the internet playing a major role, but in a much larger scale. The entertainment industry's relentless exploitation of young women has only gotten worse too, with Katseye being a recent example of this constant and needles sexualization of people who're still trying to find their feet. Rumi's character is so interesting to me. I wholeheartedly believe that her idol persona came from a place of concern, but the deep seated resentment for how her own career turned out to be seeped into those concerns, twisting it into a complete breakdown of her sense of self. Victims of a system who should do nothing but beg for forgiveness and disappear completely.

I knew Rumi was up to something this whole time, and can I just point out how behind every beautiful talented women in the industry, there’s always going to be a sick perverted stalker unfortunately. Overall, this film confused me but I think in the end, Mima is basically coming in terms with her true identity. Which is just Mima, not idol Mima or actress Mima. I would also like to point how I instantly thought of the artwork Agnus by Konstantin Korobov while watching this film.

Satoshi Kon is the fcking goat. There is so much great stuff to point out here but i just want to highlight how brilliantly the film blends frames into each other creating these seemless transitions that take you from one place to another so far removed from where you started without you noticing it. This of course adds to the effort the film puts into blurring the line between reality and illusion.

Thank you Maddie the goat for suggesting me to watch this master piece This is easily in my top 3 movies I’ve ever watched.The first 10minutes of the film are obv slow, but after the film is insane, the constant tripping in and out of reality is amazing to even see, the constant match cuts from reality and  fantasy in Mima’s bedroom is BRILLIANT, the representation of degradation in acting during the late 90s is displayed so well, admittedly the rape scene is extremely disturbing, but it makes sense due to what it’s meant to symbolise. Just the fact that the director is able to use mental illness in such a way (dissociative identity disorder) for rumi is super creative, Re-mania being manipulated by Rumi is also really intuitive to show how realistic rumi’s perception of being Mima actually was, an obsessed stalker falling victim to his own interest, also the use of music in the car park where Shibuya dies, the Cham song being played the lyrics were absolute genius talking about loves grasp on people and using aggression to make an advancement in that sense revealing to use subtly how Re-mania is willing to take his obsession to any length to get closer to Mima, also the mental health deteriorating slowly is really good I personally believe Rumi was used as a symbol to show Mima’s prerequisite moral of staying pure and the scene where she starts crying like crazy after the rape scene shows this very clearly using Rumi. And finally the last 10second scene summing up how Mima is back to normal imo is kinda wasted she seems entirely fine and no effect on her mental health I feel that should’ve left a mental scar on her for life or maybe the point of that is to show that her mental health is fully gone and she is now moving through life as if nothing happened to show she’s numbing her real feeling again, But overall 5/5 film will defo be rewatching this lol

I've never tried ayahuasca but I imagine this is what it would feel like. A film that disorients and leaves you wondering what was real and what was imagined. I'd argue that's the beauty of Perfect Blue, it immerses the viewer and traps them in the very psychosis that Mima experiences. The movie blips brilliantly in and out of her scenes as an actress, and mixes with her everyday life that's corrupted by a menacing online presence and public backlash that leaves Mima no longer knowing who she is and thus as a viewer we too are left just as dazed and confused as she is.

Hence the cultural artifact comment, it’s a story from a different time. Old Criminal Minds episodes come to mind actually now that I think abt it. Weebs won!
